name: SO-101
description: A 3D-printed, 6-joint desktop robot arm designed by The Robot Studio in collaboration with Hugging Face, built around low-cost Feetech bus servos. Used in matched leader/follower pairs for teleoperated imitation-learning research — a human demonstrates a task by hand-guiding the leader arm while the follower's motions and camera feed are logged as training data. The current flagship of this arm family, directly succeeding SO-100: the leader arm now ships with naturally lower-torque, factory-backdrivable servo variants, eliminating SO-100's gear-pulling modification entirely.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: no official figure found in this research

specs.label: Software
specs.note: Apache-2.0; trains ACT, SmolVLA, and other imitation-learning policies

specs.label: Degrees of Freedom
specs.note: 5 arm joints (base, shoulder, elbow, wrist pitch, wrist roll) + 1 gripper axis

specs.label: Payload
specs.note: third-party estimate — no official payload, reach, or repeatability spec published

specs.label: Actuators
specs.note: follower keeps standard 1/345 gearing (or a 12V/30kg·cm "Pro" variant); leader uses factory lower-torque ratios instead — no more gear-pulling

specs.label: Status
specs.note: supersedes SO-100, whose own docs are now marked deprecated

specs.label: Construction
specs.note: PLA/PLA+; individual per-part STL files (vs. SO-100's print trays); revised wiring addresses a joint-3 disconnection issue

specs.label: Teleop Method
specs.note: leader ships naturally backdrivable out of the box — no servo disassembly needed, unlike SO-100

specs.label: Host Interface
specs.note: required USB-C-to-servo-bus board, visible at this arm's base; needs its own separate DC power input

specs.label: Creator
specs.note: Rob Knight; kit manufacturing now also involves Seeed Studio, WowRobo, and PartaBot

sourcing: Specs compiled from the official TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100 GitHub repository (including its README, BOM tables, per-model STL folders, and LICENSE file), Hugging Face's official LeRobot documentation for SO-101, Seeed Studio's kit listings, and independent coverage (TechCrunch, ThinkRobotics, OpenELAB, DeepWiki) as of this build. SO-101 supersedes SO-100 directly, so this page replaces what was previously this catalog's standalone SO-100 entry — SO-100 is now described here as SO-101's predecessor. Exact per-joint leader-servo gear ratios and reach/payload figures vary slightly or are unofficial across sources; see Worth Knowing above for specifics. Pricing varies by sourcing method (raw BOM vs. assembled kit) — see Reference Price above.

pricing.summary: Pricing is essentially unchanged from SO-100: the project's own bill-of-materials still prices a complete leader+follower teleoperation pair at roughly **$230** in parts, while Seeed Studio sells electronics-only kits at **$220** for the standard version or **$240** for a "Pro" variant. Fully assembled kits from resellers are reported anywhere from roughly $100 to $500 depending on assembly level and shipping/tariffs — a wide range that isn't consistently corroborated across sources, so treat the top end cautiously.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: SO-101 isn't a Hugging Face design any more than SO-100 was — both come from Rob Knight of The Robot Studio, with Hugging Face's role limited to software integration via its `lerobot` library, not the hardware itself. Reach and payload figures commonly quoted around 500mm and 500g are third-party estimates only; neither Hugging Face nor the GitHub repo publishes official reach, payload, or repeatability figures for SO-100 or SO-101.
